CUPID: Biggest winner, but the textbook signals were weak at entry. It bottomed with the market on 7-Apr. At the breakout, the latest quarter (Mar-25) showed net profit down 50%, so price led the numbers. The next three quarters then grew profit 88%, 140% and 200%. This is a 'price first, earnings later' example: you had to trust relative strength and volume.
QPOWER: Listed Feb-2025, so there is no 200-day history. It made a post-IPO base, bottomed on 7-Apr, and broke out on 7.9× volume in May. Revenue grew 119–290% YoY through 2025. This is the post-IPO-base pattern: a fresh listing, a first base and a high-volume breakout.
IFBAGRO: Very thin stock (about ₹0.15 cr/day). It broke out on 19.5× volume after moving from losses to profits. The setup was real but hard to trade in size.
SMLMAH: An event-driven move. Mahindra's purchase of a controlling stake (Apr-2025, later renamed SML Mahindra) re-rated the stock. It broke out on 16× volume. Earnings were not the trigger at the time.
ABINFRA: Thin stock. Sales rose 203% and 328% YoY in the Mar and Jun-25 quarters. RS and the trend were both already at highs when it broke out. A real earnings story, but illiquid.
LUMAXTECH: A steady compounder rather than a spike. Sales grew 20–50% YoY every quarter. It reclaimed its 52-week high on 29-May with RS at a high, then trended until December.
FORCEMOT: The cleanest setup in the list (9/9). It is liquid, profit growth accelerated (+44%, +35%, then +211% YoY), it beat the index off the low, and it cleared its 50-day high on 3.3× volume. Use this as the reference chart.
GABRIEL: RS led price. It reclaimed its 52-week high on 12× volume on 18-Mar, before the market's April retest, and profit growth held at 30–80% YoY. Stocks that make new highs while the index is still falling are the leaders.
NETWEB: AI-server theme. It fell 59% into the April low, made a V-shaped recovery, and doubled sales YoY in the Jun-25 quarter. It reclaimed its 52-week high only in September, so most of the gain came before that confirmation.
INDOTHAI: Not a crash-low story: the stock was already trending up into 2025, so the 'low' is just the first day of the year. Thin. Profit turned up from the Jun-25 quarter.
KRISHANA: Specialty chemicals. Profit rose 425% and 450% YoY in the Dec-24 and Mar-25 quarters. It reclaimed its 52-week high on 18.7× volume. The earnings were visible before the move, but liquidity was thin.
BHARATSE: NSE price history starts mid-2025, so the averages are partial. Sales grew 40–60% YoY. The breakout came 114 days after the low, the slowest in the set.
APOLLO: Defence electronics, caught in the May-2025 defence rally. It broke out on 7× volume on 9-May with very high liquidity (about ₹71 cr/day). This is the theme-plus-sector-rotation pattern.
JAYNECOIND: A 13% gap-up breakout on 28-Apr after profit turned from losses. The gap-on-results pattern.
SEJALLTD: Glass. Profit rose 100–300% YoY each quarter, so the earnings were visible. Thin trading.
AAREYDRUGS: Earnings were falling while price rose 219%, so this was a price-only move. Treat it as an outlier: the chart showed relative strength, but the fundamentals did not support it.
GRMOVER: Earliest low (13-Jan) and an early 52-week-high reclaim (3-Apr), so it held up through the market crash. Earnings were flat, then improved in the Sep and Dec quarters.
INFOBEAN: Broke out on 23.6× volume. Profit recovered in the Jun-25 quarter (+188% YoY). Thin.
SILGO: Thin jewellery stock, and Screener's quarterly history is limited. RS was strong but the earnings were not measurable.
SIGMA: Thin. Sales grew 45–50% YoY. Note: Yahoo's prices are not split-adjusted for this stock; Dhan's are.
VENUSREM: The one true long, tight base: 118 days from low to breakout, and the 10-day volume dried up to 0.85× average before the break. Profit rose 900% YoY in the Jun-25 quarter.
TFCILTD: Financial services. It broke out on 15× volume after a 54% washout. Profit grew modestly (+24% to +50%).
KMEW: Shipbuilding and dredging; short NSE history. Slow base, and it reclaimed its 52-week high only in November. A late mover.
YATRA: Turnaround: sales grew 100%+ YoY for four quarters before the move. It scores 9/9, but its 52-week-high reclaim came very late (November), so the gain was made before that confirmation.
POCL: Lead recycling. Profit grew 42–225% YoY, the stock was liquid, and it passed all 9 checks. A clean earnings-plus-RS setup.
ASHAPURMIN: Minerals. Sales and profit both rose about 90% YoY in the Jun-25 quarter. A slow grind higher, reclaiming its 52-week high in September.
GINNIFILA: Textile turnaround with a 15% gap-up on the breakout. Thin.
HLEGLAS: Earnings-gap pattern: an 18% gap-up on 20-May after the Mar-25 quarter's profit rose 113% YoY. The result was the trigger.
JSLL: Ayurveda healthcare. RS was at a 52-week high at the breakout. Yahoo's data is not split-adjusted for this stock; Dhan's is. Screener's quarterly history is short.
KIOCL: PSU iron-ore pellets with ongoing losses. A theme and policy move, not an earnings one. RS and volume carried the setup.
SINDHUTRAD: Earnings collapsed while price tripled. A price-only move with operator-style risk. Treat it as an outlier.
JINDALPHOT: Holding-company or value-unlocking situation; quarterly earnings are noisy. It broke out on 7.4× volume off a 48% washout.
NACLIND: Event-driven. Coromandel International agreed to buy a controlling stake in early 2025, and the stock broke out on 19.9× volume on 12-Mar, only 12 days after its low. That same day was also its 52-week-high reclaim, and +327% followed. Earnings were weak and erratic (Sep-25 net profit −83%), so this was a takeover re-rating, not a results story.
GRSE: Defence shipbuilder in the May-2025 defence rally. It fell 58% into the 3-Mar low and broke out on 9× volume within 17 days. The Mar-25 quarter's net profit +118% supported the move. Most of the gain came before the 52-week-high reclaim on 29-May: only +14.5% was left after it.
BANCOINDIA: Auto radiators. Earnings accelerated (Mar-25 net profit +126%), and the breakout on 19-May was a 15.7% gap-up on the results. It reclaimed its 52-week high three weeks later and still added +44%. The gap-on-results pattern.
SUVEN: Pharma R&D with no usable quarterly numbers on Screener, so the setup rests on price alone. It beat the index by 23 points to the 24-Apr breakout and reclaimed its 52-week high in mid-May, with +75% still to come.
PFOCUS: Thin (₹0.55 cr a day) media stock that bottomed with the market on 7-Apr. The breakout came quickly, but the 52-week-high reclaim waited until September. Profits swung between losses and gains, so liquidity and noise are the main risks here.
IXIGO: Travel platform. It took 70 days from the March low to break out, then reclaimed its 52-week high on 17-Jul with +59% left. The Mar-25 quarter's net profit +143% came just before the breakout. A full 9/9 score.
GODFRYPHLP: One of the earliest movers. It broke out on 12.5× volume on 17-Feb, while the market was still falling, and beat the Smallcap 250 by 75 points to the breakout. Net profit grew every quarter (+23% to +56%), so the earnings story was steady. A clean RS leader.
GMDCLTD: State mining company (lignite, with rare-earth exploration in the news in 2025). A slow base: 74 days from the March low to the 16-May breakout. Earnings were mixed until the Sep-25 quarter (+264%). Liquid, and a 9/9 score.
AXISCADES: Engineering services with defence exposure. It was already trending up into 2025: its 'low' is the first trading day of the year. The breakout and 52-week-high reclaim came together on 10-Mar, after which it doubled (+107%). Profits grew strongly throughout (Mar-25 +256%).
PARADEEP: Fertiliser maker with very strong earnings (Mar-25 net profit +682%, Jun-25 far higher). It broke out with a 5.1% gap on 8-Apr, the day after the market's retest low, and reclaimed its 52-week high a week later. The +76% that followed was earnings-backed.
STLTECH: Optical fibre maker that returned to profit in 2025. The breakout on 12-Jun was a 9.8% gap on 28.9× volume, among the heaviest volumes in the set, and it reclaimed its 52-week high days later. Most of the move came after a deep 53% washout.
HBLENGINE: Defence and railway electronics. It broke out on 7.5× volume in mid-May, but earnings only took off in the Jun and Sep-25 quarters (+79%, +345%). Price led the numbers by about a quarter. Very liquid.
TI: Tilaknagar Industries (liquor). It broke out with a 10.6% gap on 10.9× volume on 15-May after the Mar-25 quarter's net profit +148%. The July 2025 deal to buy Pernod Ricard's Imperial Blue business followed. Only +17% was left after the 52-week-high reclaim.
GALLANTT: Steel. It held up well (only a 27% fall into the late-January low), and its breakout on 1-Apr was also its 52-week-high reclaim, on 9× volume. It nearly doubled afterwards (+97%). Thin (₹0.85 cr a day), with irregular earnings.
ATHERENERG: Electric scooters, listed in May 2025, so this is a post-IPO base with no 52-week history. It broke out on 9.8× volume on 4-Aug, 89 days after the post-listing low, and doubled to the October high. Loss-making, so this was price and theme only.
GVT&D: GE Vernova T&D: power transmission equipment. The clearest earnings story in Tier 2: net profit grew 100%+ YoY in every quarter shown. It broke out on 15-May and reclaimed its 52-week high two weeks later, with +45% to come.
SHARDACROP: Agrochemicals with explosive profit growth (Dec-24 +520%, Jun-25 +430%). It broke out on 28-May and reclaimed its 52-week high on 3-Jul. The move ended quickly, on 29-Jul.
POWERINDIA: Hitachi Energy India: power transmission. Steady compounding with very strong profit growth (Jun-25 +1,220%). It beat the index by 84 points to the breakout. The breakout volume was only 1.6×, a reminder that leaders sometimes break out quietly. Very liquid.
LLOYDSENT: Holding company tied to Lloyds Metals. It broke out on 22-Apr, but never reclaimed its 52-week high before topping on 4-Jul. A short, sharp move with weak earnings at the time.
MCX: Commodity exchange in the 2025 capital-markets rally. Earnings turned around through 2024 and kept growing (Mar-25 +53%, Jun-25 +83%). It reclaimed its 52-week high a day before the formal breakout and kept trending until December (+58% after the reclaim).
CARTRADE: Online auto marketplace. It held up through the crash (only a 25% fall) and broke out on 1-Feb, just 10 days after its low, while the index was still falling. Profit growth was strong all year (+84% to +106%). A textbook early RS leader.
AIIL: Authum Investment: investment holding company. It broke out on 4.8× volume in May and reclaimed its 52-week high the next day, but reported earnings were weak. A holding-company re-rating rather than an earnings move.
JMFINANCIL: Financial services with a turnaround from losses (Mar-25 quarter back in profit, Jun-25 +146%). It broke out on 8.1× volume in mid-May. Most of the move came before the 52-week-high reclaim (only +17% after).
BSE: Exchange stock in the 2025 capital-markets rally, and the most liquid name in the study (about ₹780 cr a day). It reclaimed its 52-week high in April, before the 50-day-high breakout signal fired, so the classic sequence ran out of order here. Profits surged (Mar-25 +362%).
SYRMA: Electronics manufacturing. It broke out with a 5.5% gap on 6.6× volume on 12-May, and profits grew strongly (Dec-24 +165%, Jun-25 +150%). It reclaimed its 52-week high in July with +40% to come.
THYROCARE: Diagnostics. The breakout came on 52.5× volume, the largest volume multiple in the set, with a 7.5% gap. Earnings grew steadily (+27% to +85%). Thin (₹0.82 cr a day), and it barely beat the index into the breakout (+13 points).
RPOWER: Reliance Power, in the Anil Ambani group stocks' rally in May–June 2025. It reported profits in place of losses through 2024–25 and broke out on 9.5× volume on 23-May. The move topped within three weeks (11-Jun). Event and sentiment-driven.
YATHARTH: Hospitals. A slow build: the breakout volume was only 1.7×, profits re-accelerated from the Jun-25 quarter (+40%), and the 52-week-high reclaim came only in August. Most of the gain came before that confirmation.
INDIAGLYCO: Specialty chemicals with steady profit growth (+18% to +52%). It broke out and reclaimed its 52-week high on consecutive days in mid-May, then trended until November. Thin trading (₹1.5 cr a day).
DATAPATTNS: Defence electronics in the May-2025 defence rally. It had the deepest washout in Tier 2 (−63%) and beat the index by 52 points to the 28-Apr breakout, but never reclaimed its 52-week high before the June top.
PARAS: Defence optics and electronics, part of the May-2025 defence rally. It broke out on 14.6× volume on 28-Apr, reclaimed its 52-week high on 16-May, and topped three days later. Almost the whole move came before the reclaim.
ZENTEC: Zen Technologies: defence simulators, in the May-2025 defence rally. It fell 64% into its February low, then beat the index by 77 points to the breakout. It never reclaimed its 52-week high, and profits fell in the Jun-25 quarter (−33%). A theme bounce, not a new uptrend.
MANORAMA: Specialty fats (cocoa-butter substitutes) with profits more than doubling in late 2025. It broke out on 23-Apr and reclaimed its 52-week high five days later, with +36% to come. Screener's quarterly history is short.
SUBROS: Auto air-conditioning. A modest setup: it beat the index by only 12 points into the breakout, profit growth was mild (+6% to +53%), and the breakout volume was 2.1×. It still reclaimed its 52-week high in June and added +41%.
BDL: Bharat Dynamics: missiles, in the May-2025 defence rally. It broke out just 21 days after the March low and topped on 30-May. Earnings were weak until the Jun-25 quarter (+157%), so this was theme-driven.
TATAINVEST: Tata group investment holding company. It broke out on 8.7× volume in late May but only reclaimed its 52-week high in September. A holding-company re-rating, not an earnings story.
APARINDS: Cables and conductors. It fell 63% into the 7-Apr low, recovered quickly, but never reclaimed its 52-week high. Modest earnings growth. A recovery bounce more than a new leader.
ECLERX: Analytics services. The breakout came on 31.3× volume with a 4.8% gap on 15-May, and profit growth accelerated each quarter (+18%, +27%, +31%, +40%). It reclaimed its 52-week high in August and kept trending until December.
SANDUMA: Sandur Manganese: mining. It broke out within 22 days of its February low but only reclaimed its 52-week high in October, after a long base. Profit growth was lumpy (Dec-24 +1,422%, Sep-25 +334%).
DIACABS: Diamond Power Infrastructure: cables. The slowest breakout in the set, 128 days after the low. It topped within three weeks and never reclaimed its 52-week high. Profits surged later (Sep-25 +500%).
DBREALTY: Real estate, with a deep 60% washout. It doubled into July but had only +5% left after the 52-week-high reclaim. Earnings swung from losses to profits, so this was speculative.
INTELLECT: Banking software. It broke out on 4.8× volume a month after the 7-Apr low, reclaimed its 52-week high on 29-May, and topped three weeks later. Profit growth was uneven (Mar-25 +86%).
TRANSRAILL: Transmission EPC, listed in December 2024, so its 52-week history is short. Profits grew strongly in the Jun-25 quarter (+104%). The breakout volume was only 1.6×, and it topped in August.
COCHINSHIP: Defence shipbuilder in the May-2025 defence rally. It fell 60% into its February low and broke out on 9.2× volume in late April, but never reclaimed its 52-week high. Earnings were flat to falling. A theme bounce.
RELINFRA: Reliance Infrastructure, in the Anil Ambani group stocks' rally in May–June 2025. Profits came back from losses, it broke out on 4.7× volume on 23-May, and it topped by the end of June. Sentiment-driven.
TECHNOE: Power EPC. It broke out 14 days after the 7-Apr low but never reclaimed its 52-week high. Earnings growth faded through 2025. A recovery bounce.
MAHSCOOTER: Maharashtra Scooters: holds Bajaj group stakes. It barely beat the index into the breakout (+9.5 points), so it was not an RS leader. A holding-company re-rating that reclaimed its 52-week high in May.
SOLARINDS: Explosives and defence munitions, in the May-2025 defence rally. Steady 17–52% profit growth. The breakout on 29-Apr was also its 52-week-high reclaim; it added +33% and topped at the end of June.
DELHIVERY: Logistics, turning profitable through 2024–25. It broke out on 9.7× volume in May, but most of the move came before the 52-week-high reclaim in August (only +6% after).
GRWRHITECH: Garware Hi-Tech Films. The 'breakout' came on below-average volume (0.5×), it never reclaimed its 52-week high, and it topped two days after breaking out. Weak setup quality, with a score of 4/9.
